To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

“The global logistics system is likely to evolve in a context of a stronger integration of emerging markets in the global supply chain, with a stronger role of Europe and a strengthening of its industrial and logistics capabilities”.

the global logistics system is likely to be dominated by a SGLM model in the next 20 years and that Europe is likely to play a key role in this model, with the North African and Eastern markets playing a key role as well.

“The future of global logistics will be characterized by a symmetric model, in which local and global elements are equally important, and the European area will be characterized by strengthening of both its production and logistic capabilities, though at a different rate of development with respect with emerging economies, in a context in where North Africa and Eastern Europe play a fundamental role for production-logistics platforms”.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new strategic methodology in the field of logistics and transport and with the assessment of the impacts that the new scenario is likely to have on the European area.
the development of strategic scenarios for the future of the logistics systems worldwide, with special attention to Europe.
a strategic approach for building scenarios of future logistics systems at a global level and assessing their impacts on the European context.

the European logistics system will become more and more integrated with the rest of the global one, with the consequent increase of the importance of the European market in the world.
, in terms of global logistics, Europe will be likely to face a period of consolidation in the coming decades.

the future of global logistics will be characterised by a strong interdependence of the local/global dimension, which will be the result of a number of drivers, such as the globalisation of logistics, the emergence of new markets, new logistics technologies, and the development of logistics platforms and clusters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, while the SGLM will be likely to become the dominant model at the global level, the European logistics sector will have the opportunity to play a leading role in the development of the global logistics sector, especially in the field of logistics services and in the provision of logistics platforms for the emerging economies.

the European Union is likely to become the main logistics platform in the world, with an increasing share of logistics activities in the world economy, while at the same time it will be able to maintain its competitive edge in the global market.

Europe will have to strengthen its competitiveness by focusing on the development of a more integrated logistics sector, in which the European Union will have to act as a facilitator for the creation of a European Logistics System.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SGLM will be the most likely future scenario for the global logistics sector in the medium/long term.

Europe will need to focus on the development of a more efficient and competitive logistics infrastructure and the development of a logistics culture in its companies and institutions in order to face the challenges of global logistics and remain a competitive player in the global market.

, in a context of global economic recovery, European countries will need to focus on the strengthening of their logistics and industrial capabilities, in order to compete with emerging economies and take advantage of the new opportunities arising from the global logistics scenario.
